methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study comparing two sentinel lymph node detection methods (ICG+Patent Blue vs 99mTc+Patent Blue) over 11 years. Appropriate comparison of detection rates. No randomization; retrospective design limits causal inference. Basic statistical analysis (chi-square likely) for detection rate comparison. Sample size and power analysis not stated. Comparison confounded by temporal changes (11-year span with possible protocol evolution).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses clinically relevant question of SLN detection technique optimization in breast cancer surgery. Direct clinical application potential. Practical comparison of imaging agents in routine surgical practice. High clinical relevance to surgical oncology practice.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods adequately described for patient cohort and operative techniques. STROBE elements partially addressed. However, no statement of data availability; patient-level data not mentioned as accessible. Participant selection criteria and exclusion criteria could be more explicit. Statistical methods section minimal.

novelty_literature.justification: Incremental comparison of existing techniques with no novel methodology or new biological insights. Direct comparison of ICG and 99mTc previously published. Findings are confirmatory rather than innovative. Limited contribution to field beyond local institutional experience.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear presentation of retrospective findings with appropriate table summaries of detection rates. Methods and results sections clearly written. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within prior literature. However, relatively limited scope for a 11-year retrospective study suggests incrementalcontent.

key_strengths: Long-term single-center experience (11 years) providing substantial patient cohort
Direct clinical comparison of two common SLN detection methods
Practical relevance to surgical oncology practice
key_concerns: Purely retrospective non-randomized comparison confounded by temporal changes and protocol evolution
No power analysis or sample size justification for detection rate comparison
Novel findings absent; incremental confirmation of known technique comparisons
Limited mechanistic insight or new biological understanding
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective comparison with clinical relevance but limited novelty. Appropriate for Tier 4 with major revisions: requires either larger prospective comparison, cost-effectiveness analysis, or mechanistic investigation to increase impact.
